line: One column holds the whole thing up. Its architect said it rises from the water like a flower.
Legend says it has 9,999 rooms, one short of heaven's 10,000. A survey counted 8,886.
More than a million tiles cover it, and they clean themselves when it rains.
Its name means 'the red one', after the colour of its walls.
Every terrace is the roof of the flat below. Its architect still keeps one of them.
Asked why it was taking so long, its architect said his client was not in a hurry.
It was meant to stand for just six months. That was in 1958.
Inside, the atrium is shaped like a single grain of corn, blown up to fill the building.
An 82-metre curved escalator carries you up through an old warehouse to a plaza in the sky.

line: Its name means 'beautiful spring', after a well whose water was drunk by the imperial court.

cfg.clue: A 2,000-year-old temple behind a porch of granite columns. The open eye at the top of its concrete dome lets the rain fall straight onto the floor.

line: Nearly 2,000 years old, and still the largest unreinforced concrete dome on Earth.
